Salesforce (CRM) stock has gained 10.9% since the day before the company raised its fiscal 2027 profit forecast on August 26, 2026, outpacing a 1.1% return for the S&P 500. Yet a raised forecast is merely a projection of future performance. Investors must ask if the market is still buying into that promise today. Is that gain still building, or did it all come in the first two days.
The broader trend remains upward, however. Salesforce trades 1.8% above its 50-day average, which represents the average closing price over the last 50 trading days. It also sits 14.4% above its 200-day average. When a stock price stays above both benchmarks, with the shorter average tracking higher, the chart signals a clear uptrend. Even so, Salesforce is now holding only just above its 50-day average. What Salesforce Management Raised Management raised its fiscal 2027 guide for earnings per share to $10.21 to $10.25, from an earlier midpoint of $7.96. Most of that guidance increase is already accounted for: second-quarter GAAP earnings per share surged to $4.29 against a $1.75 guide, boosted by discrete non-operating gains while operating income remained essentially flat with the first quarter. It is important to note this is a revised forecast for the same year, rather than a final result. The sales forecast shifted far less. Salesforce now expects fiscal 2027 revenue of $46.1 billion to $46.4 billion, sitting just 0.4% above its prior guide at the midpoint.

Revenue increased 11% year-over-year (YoY) to $11.3 billion, while subscription and support revenue, Salesforce’s core revenue stream, rose 12% to $10.8 billion. Cash generation was notably stronger, with operating cash flow rising 71% to $1.3 billion and free cash flow increasing 81% to $1.1 billion. AI remained a major focus of the quarter. Agentforce and Data 360 ARR reached nearly $3.9 billion, up more than 210% YoY, while Agentforce ARR exceeded $1.5 billion, representing growth of more than 240%. Salesforce also reported 3.2 billion Agentic Work Units delivered during the quarter and said Data 360 processed 104 trillion records, up 355% YoY. These metrics provide additional context for investors assessing whether Salesforce’s AI investments are translating into measurable commercial adoption.

exa-lite.snippet:
Mara Voss · 27 August 2026 at 14:19 UTC · Reading Time 7 min · Last update: 27 August 2026

...

Salesforce’s latest income statement contains two almost motionless numbers and one spectacular one.

GAAP operating income was US$2.331 billion in the fiscal second quarter. A year earlier it was US$2.332 billion. Yet diluted GAAP earnings per share rose from US$1.96 to US$4.29, an increase of 119%.

Both figures are correct. They answer different questions.

Operating income measures what remained after the cost of delivering, developing, selling and administering Salesforce’s products. EPS continued below that line, where a US$2.613 billion gain on strategic investments entered the quarter. It then divided net income by 821 million diluted shares, 141 million fewer than a year earlier.

...

## The US$2.43 below the operating line

Revenue rose 10.8% to US$11.345 billion and gross profit rose to US$8.696 billion. Those are meaningful gains. Operating expenses also increased, while gross margin slipped by roughly one percentage point. The result was an operating margin of 20.5%, compared with about 22.8% a year earlier, and essentially no growth in operating income.
